title: The Amazing Life of Christine Granville
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck profile Christine Granville (born Krystyna Skarbek), a Polish-born British SOE agent in World War Two. They cover her aristocratic, financially declining youth in Poland, her smuggling and skiing routes over the Tatra Mountains into Hungary, her recruitment by SOE (Special Operations Executive) under George Taylor, her cover roles, her marriages and affairs including with Andrzej Kowerski, her wartime exploits in France and Italy, her rescue of resistance prisoners in August 1944 by bribery, her postwar struggles to find work, and her murder in 1950s by a jealous former coworker, Dennis Muldowney. The episode closes with a discussion of biographies and a film about her, followed by listener mail (a request from a ten-year-old named Henry about dark walls making rooms feel smaller) and off-topic movie chat.
topics: Claire Mullen biography The Spy Who Loved

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and the intro speaker tease the story of a woman spy from Poland in World War Two.

segments.title: Listener suggestion and introduction to Christine Granville
segments.summary: Josh credits listener Jen Spota of Seattle with suggesting the episode. The hosts introduce Christine Granville as a British wartime spy, born Christina Skarbek, and her aristocratic family background.

segments.title: Family, youth and the Goldfelder bank
segments.summary: Her mother came from the Jewish Goldfelder banking family. After World War One the bank failed and her father left and died, leaving the family with little money. She lived a high life, ran in beauty contests, and smuggled cigarettes with criminals near a ski resort.

segments.title: Joining SOE
segments.summary: After Germany invaded Poland, Granville approached George Taylor of SOE, offering to work with the Polish resistance. The hosts describe SOE's use of civilian volunteers for sabotage, including the Panzer train grease sabotage.

segments.title: Cover roles and skiing across the Alps
segments.summary: Granville proposed operating from Hungary and skiing over the Tatra Mountains into Poland. She was given cover as a first aid nursing yeomanry member and a flight officer in the British Women's Auxiliary Air Force. She crossed the mountains with Olympic skier Jan Mauritz Arts, reportedly passing frozen bodies.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break.

segments.title: Myths versus documented stories
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how some of Granville's stories are hard to separate from myth, and describe a train episode where she hid illegal documents in a box given to a Gestapo officer.

segments.title: Relationship with Kowerski and romantic pursuers
segments.summary: Granville met Andrzej Kowerski, a one-legged Polish war hero and spy, and had a lifelong on-and-off relationship with him while still married. A former suitor in Budapest reportedly shot himself in the foot when she refused to return.

segments.title: Her mother, the Musketeers, and the Nazi invasion warning
segments.summary: Her mother was killed after being captured while teaching at a secret school. Granville worked with the Musketeers resistance group in Poland. She reportedly warned British intelligence of the German invasion of the Soviet Union, which happened on the day predicted. Churchill called her his favorite spy.

segments.title: Budapest prison and tongue-biting escape
segments.summary: In January 1941 Granville and Kowerski were arrested by Hungarian police. She feigned tuberculosis by biting her tongue and coughing blood, and they were released. The hosts mention a Budapest museum on the former interrogation site and the Hospital in the Rock.

segments.title: New identities and Polish intelligence rivalry
segments.summary: After their cover was blown, she took the name Christine Granville and Kowerski became Andrew Kennedy. Polish intelligence accused them of being double agents, a dispute rooted in SOE's conflicting instructions. Her former husband Jerzy Giziycki resigned in protest. They were cleared after a year in Cairo.

segments.title: France mission and wartime tactics
segments.summary: In July 1944 she parachuted into southern France as Pauline Armand, working with Francis Cammaerts's SOE independent French section. The hosts describe her weapons and disguises, a bluff with grenades at the Italian border, a silk map hidden in a headscarf, and a German shepherd story.

segments.title: Cliffhanger break
segments.summary: Hosts tease the next story and take a break.

segments.title: Rescue of resistance prisoners by bribery
segments.summary: In August 1944 Granville posed as the niece of General Montgomery to persuade a French prison's captors to spare Cammaerts and other resistance members, paying two million francs. The SOE reportedly praised her report.

segments.title: Postwar honors and neglect
segments.summary: Granville received the Officer of the Order of the British Empire and the George Medal, and the French Croix de Guerre. Despite these honors, the British government cut her financial support and struggled to find her work, a situation the hosts link to Churchill losing power and rivalry with professional intelligence.

segments.title: Later jobs and Ian Fleming rumor
segments.summary: She worked as a housekeeper, switchboard operator and cruise ship waitress. A rumor holds that she inspired Vesper Lynd in Casino Royale through an affair with Ian Fleming.

segments.title: Murder by Dennis Muldowney
segments.summary: Granville was stabbed to death in the lobby of a Polish Relief Society boarding house by Dennis Muldowney, a former cruise ship coworker who was obsessed with her.

segments.title: Legacy, biographies and Kowerski's later life
segments.summary: Kowerski, known as Kennedy, died in 1988 and was buried with Granville in London. Friends blocked scandalous biographies for a time. Claire Mullen's 2012 biography The Spy Who Loved is described as definitive.

segments.title: Film adaptations and celebrity tangent
segments.summary: The hosts mention a film called Partisan with Morgane Polanski as Granville, and a tangent about Malcolm McDowell, Andie McDowell and Roddy McDowell that they resolve only partly.

segments.title: Movie recommendations
segments.summary: Hosts discuss movies including Made, Sanctuary, and The Hill, and the 1979 Disney film The Black Hole.

segments.title: Listener mail from Henry
segments.summary: Ten-year-old Henry asks for an episode on how dark wall colors make a room feel smaller. The hosts suggest a short on how color affects perceived size.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to send email and close the show.
